draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Jog Falls! The Sharavati River plunges about 253 m here and splits into four cascades named Raja, Rani, Roarer and Rocket, making it the third-highest waterfall in India.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have named food spots for Jog, so ask around Jog-Kargal town for a simple meal.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Christ the King Church is a 2 min walk, and the front panoramic viewpoint in Jog-Kargal gives you the full view of the falls.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Pick a spot at the front panoramic viewpoint and watch the four cascades for a while.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Jog is ranked 36th in the list of the world's highest free-falling waterfalls.

spots.name: Jog Falls

tips.title: The rain changes the show.
tips.body: Depending on rainfall and season, the segmented falls can turn into one big plunge.

tips.title: Try both viewpoints.
tips.body: There's the front panoramic viewpoint in Jog-Kargal, and the British Bungalow viewpoint right beside the falls in Siddapur taluk.

story.title: Many names
story.body: The falls go by many names, Gerusoppa Falls, Joga Jalapata and Jogada Gundi among them. The Sharavati River drops a total of 253 m here.

story.title: A church by the falls
story.body: Christ the King Church was established at Jog Falls in 1959.

story.title: On the world list
story.body: Jog is the third-highest waterfall in India and ranks 36th among the world's highest free-falling waterfalls on the World Waterfall Database.
